Hi Sarah — great questions and thanks for the quick note. Below is a concise summary of Redwood defaults and the configuration options we discussed on the call. I'm including Rishi (security lead) and Dev (product infra) to weigh in if you'd like more technical detail or evidence for your security questionnaire.

Summary — default behavior and options (short):
- Are prompts/outputs stored? Default: yes, we persist request/response logs to support debugging, quality monitoring, and customer support.
- Where are they stored? By default logs are stored in the customer tenant in the region you select when creating the workspace (for hosted: e.g., us-east-1). We can also configure EU regions for EU customers.
- What is retained and for how long? Default retention: 30 days for full request/response logs (prompts + outputs). Aggregated/derived analytics (usage metrics, token counts, anonymized quality metrics) retained 13 months.
- Raw audio/transcripts: If you pass audio to a speech-to-text preprocessor we persist the transcript as part of request logs by default. Audio files are not stored by default unless you enable an explicit artifact storage option — we recommend disabling audio storage if you want no binary artifacts retained.
- Disable logging: Yes — you can opt out of request/response logging at the workspace level ("no-log" mode). In that mode, we do not persist prompts or outputs to our hosted logs; ephemeral in-memory handling occurs during inference and only aggregated metrics are kept (unless you explicitly enable additional telemetry).
- Private deployment: If your requirement is zero telemetry to Redwood cloud, our Private option (VPC or on-prem) gives you full control — no logs are sent to Redwood control plane; retention is customer-managed.
- Encryption & keys: Data at rest is encrypted with customer-managed keys (KMS) for Dedicated/Private; hosted uses Redwood-managed KMS by default but we support customer KMS for enterprise contracts.
- Access & audit: All request logs are access-controlled and audited. We can provide search/export for allowed personnel and integrate with your SIEM via secure streaming.

Attached: redwood-data-retention.pdf (short summary) and a DPA draft.

Next steps I suggest: 1) confirm whether you need workspace-level no-log, or full Private deployment; 2) if workspace no-log is acceptable, we can provide a small pilot with no retained prompts for 30 days; 3) if Private is required, we can fast-track a technical workshop.

If useful I can provide explicit answers for each line of your security questionnaire.

Thanks — Neha

Hi Sarah — adding a few technical clarifications from the security perspective: 

- Storage model: Request/response logs are stored in encrypted object storage per workspace. Each workspace maps to a tenant bucket in the selected region (e.g., s3://redwood-logs-us-east-1/acmehealth-workspace-123). We can provide customer-managed KMS for encryption and ensure keys never leave your account for Dedicated/Private.
- Retention controls: Retention is configurable per workspace; default 30 days, min configurable down to 0 days (immediate deletion) with a 24-hour eventual consistency window. Deletion is a soft-delete followed by secure purge based on your retention policy.
- Redaction: We offer automated prompt/output redaction pipelines that can remove or mask PII fields before persistence. Redaction rules can be based on entity types (SSN, PHI, email) or prompt patterns; we can apply Q/A and NER-based filters prior to storage.
- Audit & export: Full audit trails for access, exportable via our Console or API. We can push logs to your SIEM (e.g., Splunk) through an encrypted forwarder.
- Evidence: happy to provide screenshots and an export sample for your audit team.

I'll follow up with the exact API calls and the retention-setting endpoint if you'd like to test.

— Rishi

Sarah — quick bullets below and I've attached the DPA with the EU residency clause flagged. Full written evidence pack (screenshots, retention API call examples, redact-sample) attached if you need it for legal review.

Answers: 
1) No-log workspace: Confirmed in writing — when workspace-level no-log is enabled, request/response payloads (prompts and outputs) are not persisted to storage. They are processed in-memory for inference and are not written to logs, object storage, or analytics pipelines. We will provide a signed statement as part of the contract addendum if needed.
2) Redaction example: raw prompt: "Patient SSN: 123-45-6789. Please summarize."
   stored payload (redacted): "Patient SSN: [REDACTED_SSN]. Please summarize."
   We can also hash or tokenize the SSN instead of redaction per your preference; sample pipeline included in the evidence pack.
3) DPA & EU residency: The DPA draft supports selecting EU-hosted storage and includes a configurable retention clause. The 0-day retention option is available for Private deployments and for hosted workspaces via the retention API (min 0 days, subject to eventual consistency/purge window).

Let me know if procurement wants the signed addendum and we'll route it via our legal team. Happy to set up a short call between your legal/security and our compliance team tomorrow.

Thanks — Neha
Neha Kapoor
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
